behavioral_notes.observation: The public /event and /events routes (http, auth=public, website=True, sitemap=sitemap_event) render the website_event.index page. They build the catalog via website._search_with_fuzzy('events', ...) and _read_group facet counts by date / tag (event.tag) / type (event.type) / country, paginated 12 per page with website.pager. GET requests on multi-tag URLs are 301-redirected to /event to stop crawler combinatorial explosion. This frontend search+facet behaviour lives in the controller, not in metadata.

/event/<event> redirects either to the event's first menu child URL (event.menu_id.child_id) or to /event/<id>/register. /event/<event>/register renders website_event.event_description_full with open slots (event_slot_ids._filter_open_slots) and Google Calendar / iCal resource URLs (event._get_event_resource_urls). Both are auth=public readonly routes, exposing the backend event.event record as a public registration page.

The POST confirm route is the bridge's core write: it verifies the website_event_registration reCAPTCHA token, parses the attendee form (_process_attendees_form -> name/email/phone/company_name + event.question answers), re-checks seat availability via event._verify_seats_availability (raising ValidationError -> redirect with registration_error_code=insufficient_seats), then _create_attendees_from_registration_post calls env['event.registration'].sudo().create(...) stamping event_id, partner_id and the website.visitor (visitor_id). On success it redirects to /registration/success. So an anonymous website visitor creates real event.registration rows in the event module. Not visible in metadata.

Toggling website_menu (or the introduction/register/community sub-menu booleans) creates or unlinks a root website.menu plus per-event website.event.menu rows and their ir.ui.view pages on the fly; menus_update_by_field drives selective sync. Publishing/unpublishing an event thus mutates the live website navigation tree -- an automation side-effect invisible to the schema.

is_participating is computed by a heuristic that reads the current website.visitor (_get_visitor_from_request) and/or the logged partner, then _read_groups event.registration in state open/done to decide if the viewer already registered. This couples the public page render to event.registration + website.visitor state and personalises the CTA; the logic is Python, not metadata.

The website model is extended so site search and the configurator know about events: _search_get_details appends event.event._search_get_detail for search_type in ['events','all'], get_suggested_controllers/get_cta_data wire an 'Events' entry and a /event call-to-action, and new_page() wraps event/* pages in the website_event.layout template and re-keys the view per event. This is the website<->event bridging glue.

17 JS files / 5 XML templates implement the registration UX as website public.interactions (events list filtering, event_page, modal_registration, slot_details, ticket_details, display_timer countdown, register_toaster) plus a NewContentSystrayItem patch to create an event from the website editor; no OWL components. event._get_event_resource_urls emits an outbound https://www.google.com/calendar/render? add-to-calendar link (and a local /event/<id>/ics iCal URL). Entirely client-side / static, outside Python metadata.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_event is the BRIDGE module that fuses two value networks: it turns website (the network/mediating web-presence platform) into the public online registration channel for event (the network that mediates organizer<->attendee around seat capacity). It is itself a value network (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology): its reason to exist is to connect an open population of website visitors to events and let them join -- publishing events as SEO pages, operating the catalog/search facets, and running the self-service /event/<id>/register -> /registration/confirm flow that creates event.registration rows from anonymous visitors (visitor_id link). The economic logic is membership/mediation (online seat sign-up, add-to-calendar, visitor matching), not a sequential input->output transformation (chain) nor case-by-case problem solving (shop). activity_class is primary because online event marketing & registration is a customer-facing demand activity, not back-office support. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell is the closest PCF home (over 6.0 Manage Customer Service) because the bridge's purpose is the public market/sell motion -- publishing and registering attendees to a marketed event -- inheriting the same 3.0 placement as both event and website; post-sale service flows are not its concern.

per-event published website page (SEO metadata, cover image, visibility public/link/logged)

marketing-driven event landing pages with SEO and website-builder snippets
